vulnerability_analysis: The CoinToken contract's updateUniswapV2Router() function lacks proper validation of the new router address. An attacker (as owner) can set a malicious router that returns fake factory and WETH addresses, allowing them to control the uniswapV2Pair address through the createPair() call. Combined with setAutomatedMarketMakerPair(), this allows setting arbitrary pair addresses as automated market makers.
attack_strategy: 1. Deploy a malicious router contract that returns attacker-controlled addresses. 2. As owner, call updateUniswapV2Router() with the malicious router. 3. Call setAutomatedMarketMakerPair() with attacker-controlled pair address. 4. Verify uniswapV2Pair is now attacker-controlled.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy MaliciousRouter contract with controllable factory and WETH addresses. 2. Impersonate owner using vm.prank(). 3. Call updateUniswapV2Router(maliciousRouter). 4. Call setAutomatedMarketMakerPair(attackerPair, true). 5. Assert that CoinToken.uniswapV2Pair() == attackerPair.
